headline: 劇場與有聲書新評論
context: 倫敦西區新推出的音樂劇《猜火車》（Trainspotting）評價不理想，被形容像是丹尼．鮑伊（Danny Boyle）原版電影的黯淡翻版。同一時間，作家麥特．海格（Matt Haig）的新作有聲書《午夜列車》（The Midnight Train）倒是收穫了溫暖的書評。

sources.name: The Guardian
sources.summary: Theatre Royal Haymarket, London The chopped-up story means this ends up feeling like a weak impersonation of Danny Boyle’s classic film “Choose life …” Those iconic words from that era-defining film are said more than once in this musical take on Irvine Welsh’s novel about Renton and his renegade gang of smackheads from Leith. “Choose being in the moment,” says the disembodied voice that asks us to switch off our mobile phones before the show has begun (with, one imagines, a self-satisfied glint at the joke). “Choose life,” repeats Renton (Lewis Kidd), trying so hard, it seems, to capture the dangerous energy of that moment in the 1990s when Ewan McGregor, Jonny Lee Miller and co depicted heroin addiction as a protest against the grunting conventions of ordinary life. sources.name: The New York Times
sources.summary: If the 1996 cult classic film was a high for a generation of moviegoers, a new London stage production feels like the comedown.
sources.title: ‘Trainspotting: The Musical’: When the Lust for Life Is Gone

sources.name: The Guardian
sources.summary: Actor James Norton brings a sense of gentle longing to this tale of an octogenarian looking back on the life he’s departed The latest novel from the Reasons to Stay Alive author Matt Haig begins with an octogenarian man having a heart attack. Former business magnate Wilbur Budd is already feeling a bit peculiar when he receives a phone call from his ex-wife, Maggie, who he hasn’t heard from in years. “I wanted to hear your voice,” she tells him wistfully. Minutes after getting off the phone, Wilbur collapses on his front lawn and dies. What sounds like the end of a story is, in fact, the beginning as Wilbur finds himself standing on a train platform with his mind “reverberating as if from some giant cosmic cymbal crash”. A train arrives and a woman disembarks and introduces herself as Agnes. She is, she says, the ghost of a bookseller who once ran a shop Wilbur visited as a child. She will be guiding him in a voyage through his past, pausing at formative moments including his brother’s premature death and Wilbur and Maggie’s honeymoon in Venice. “This is death,” Agnes tells him. “Where your life flashes before your eyes. This is how it happens. Fast and slow. Like life … ” Continue reading...

劇場與有聲書新評論

倫敦西區新推出的音樂劇《猜火車》（Trainspotting）評價不理想，被形容像是丹尼．鮑伊（Danny Boyle）原版電影的黯淡翻版，歌曲也讓人記不住。同一時間，作家麥特．海格（Matt Haig）的新作有聲書《午夜列車》（The Midnight Train）倒是收穫了溫暖書評，演員詹姆斯．諾頓（James Norton）的朗讀被讚有溫度。

—— 本則來自 The Guardian、The New York Times，2026 年 7 月 23 日發佈，讓圖書館員翻譯給你聽。

劇場與有聲書新評論

倫敦西區新推出的音樂劇《猜火車》（Trainspotting）評價不理想，被形容像是丹尼．鮑伊（Danny Boyle）原版電影的黯淡翻版，歌曲也讓人記不住。同一時間，作家麥特．海格（Matt Haig）的新作有聲書《午夜列車》（The Midnight Train）倒是收穫了溫暖書評，演員詹姆斯．諾頓（James Norton）的朗讀被讚有溫度。

本則整理自 The Guardian 與 The New York Times 於 2026 年 7 月 23 日發佈的報導。
voice_text: 劇場與有聲書，這邊有兩則新評論。倫敦西區的音樂劇《猜火車》評價不理想，被說像是原版電影的黯淡翻版，歌曲也讓人記不住。另一頭，作家麥特．海格（Matt Haig）的新作有聲書《午夜列車》，倒是收穫了溫暖的書評，朗讀者的詮釋被讚有溫度。
